draft.title: Mental health as a priority
card: Mental health conditions, such as anxiety and depression, are common in Australia. Many people will have one at some point in their lives.
Many conditions first appear in adolescence and young adulthood. This is one reason young people are a focus for mental health programs.
Mental health conditions are a leading cause of illness in Australia. They can affect study, work, relationships and physical health.
Early support can reduce how serious a condition becomes. Stigma is negative judgement about mental illness, and it can stop people seeking help. Reducing stigma makes it easier to ask for support.
draft.remember: Mental health is a priority because it is common, starts young and causes much illness, and early support and less stigma help.

a.q: Why does reducing stigma help improve mental health outcomes?
opts: People are more willing to seek support early
People no longer develop mental health conditions
Conditions stop appearing in young people
Early support becomes unnecessary for most people
a.why: Stigma is negative judgement, and it can stop people asking for help. When it falls, people are more likely to seek support early. It does not prevent conditions from starting, so the other options go too far.
a.clue: Think about what stigma stops people from doing.

b.q: A school in Bathurst finds that many students first report anxiety in Years 9 and 10. It starts a program where students can talk to a counsellor without fear of being judged. Which reason best supports this as a priority action?
opts: Conditions often start young, and early support helps
Anxiety only affects students and not adults
Counselling removes the risk of any later illness
Mental health conditions are rare, so they need attention
b.why: The card says many conditions start in young people and that early support can reduce how serious they become. Counselling cannot remove all risk, and the claim that conditions are rare is wrong because they are common.
b.clue: Link when conditions often begin to when help should start.

a.best: People are more willing to seek support early

b.best: Conditions often start young, and early support helps

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a hedged qualifier ('often'). Every distractor uses an absolute or plainly false claim ('any later illness', 'only affects students', 'rare'), so a student could pick the answer by elimination without knowing the idea.
The distractors are obviously false even to a student who has not read the card, so the question is too easy for Year 12 HSC students.

check.summary: The card and the facts are accurate, and question a is sound. In question b, the right answer is the only hedged option among plainly absolute distractors, so it is easy to spot without knowing the idea, and the question is too easy for Year 12.

b.q: A school in Bathurst finds many students first report anxiety in Years 9 and 10. It sets up counselling where students can talk without fear of being judged. How does this program act on the card's ideas?
opts: It gives help early and makes students less afraid to ask
It reduces stigma, which is the main cause of anxiety
It stops anxiety starting by making students less afraid
It waits until anxiety is serious, when help works best
